answer: An auditor observes that each epoch is scored along a spiral: the registry samples a growing share of low-history accounts, tightening the ring until confidence is met. Violations are recorded as timestamped entries when an account fails to present work at the jetty, the single intake where a signed deliverable must land. A sonnet-length proof is also required, a fixed-format statement each account composes itself, so copies are caught by stylistic drift. An operator farming accounts pays for every sampled failure, while a genuine account is rarely audited.
